title: go.mod declares go 1.21 but tests use go1.23+ API httptest.NewRequestWithContext
evidence: go.mod:3 says `go 1.21`; main_test.go:24,41,64,79,105,120,140,166,174 call httptest.NewRequestWithContext (added in go1.23). `go vet ./...` emits 9 diagnostics: 'httptest.NewRequestWithContext requires go1.23 or later (module is go1.21)'. This is the entire defect_rate signal: 9 defects / 512 LOC * 1000 = 17.58/kloc -> defect_rate 0.6484 (matches scores.json). Build+tests passed only because the eval toolchain is >= go1.23; on the declared go1.21 the test package would not compile and the run would fail the test gate.
suggestion: Bump the go.mod directive to `go 1.23` (or use httptest.NewRequest, which needs no version bump), so the declared minimum matches the API actually used.

title: Duplicate/empty ISBN returns 500 instead of a 4xx
evidence: database.go migrate(): `isbn TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`. ISBN is optional per spec (only title+author are validated in handlers.go validateCreateBook). Creating two books without an isbn, or with the same isbn, violates the UNIQUE constraint; CreateBook/UpdateBook return the raw error and handlers.go handleError maps any non-ErrNotFound error to 500 internal server error rather than 400/409.
suggestion: Either drop the UNIQUE/NOT NULL constraint on isbn, or detect the constraint violation and return 400/409 with a clear message.

title: GET /health is implemented but not exercised by any test
evidence: main.go registers a /health handler returning {"status":"ok"} with 200 (R10 satisfied), but main_test.go has no test hitting /health. It is one reason statement coverage sits at 62.1% rather than higher (the server bootstrap in main.go is also uncovered).
suggestion: Add a small test asserting GET /health returns 200 and {"status":"ok"}.
